description: A source code analyzer built for surfacing features of interest and other characteristics to answer the question 'What's in the code?' quickly using static analysis with a json based rules engine. Ideal for scanning components before use or detecting feature level changes.

summary.one_liner: Microsoft Application Inspector is a static source code characterization tool that reports what features and coding characteristics a codebase contains (crypto, file operations, shell calls, cloud APIs, frameworks) using a JSON rules engine.
summary.what_it_does: Scans source files, directories, or compressed archives (.tgz, .zip) against a set of over 400 feature-detection rules built from library/API calls and regex patterns. It reports what the code does rather than labeling patterns as good or bad. It supports many languages including C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Python, Go, Ruby and PowerShell, and can handle mixed-language projects. Output can be HTML (the default), JSON, text, SARIF, or Markdown. The CLI also includes commands to compare tags between two source paths, export rule tags, verify custom rule syntax, and pack rule files.
use_cases: vet third-party or open source components before use
detect feature-level changes between component versions
find cryptography or other security-relevant features in code
add a feature-inventory check to a build pipeline
generate SARIF or Markdown reports for CI
build a metadata repository of enterprise application features
notable: Reports what code does without judging good or bad patterns
Over 400 feature-detection rules, extendable with custom rules
Outputs HTML, JSON, text, SARIF, and Markdown
Usable as a .NET global tool, platform binary, or C# library on NuGet
Supports feature-delta comparison between versions via tagdiff
caveats: Requires .NET 6.0 or later for the .NET Core version
Supported platforms listed as Windows, Linux, or macOS
Rules are pattern-based, so results describe detected features rather than verified behavior
